Subject: Work sample handoff: prompt, rubric, and reviewer scheduling

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for interviewing with us. As discussed, attached is the work sample prompt and the grading rubric. Please treat this as a take-home diagnostic: the goal is to see architecture thinking, trade-off discussion, and a short prototype (if applicable).

Key details:
- Deliverable: short write-up (1–2 pages) + code prototype (if helpful).
- Deadline: EOD Monday, 2027-02-08 PT (we can accommodate a brief extension if needed).
- Submit by replying to this thread and attaching your files (zip or link).

Attachments included: work-sample.pdf (assignment prompt), grading-rubric.xlsx (what reviewers will score). If you prefer to share a Drive link, that works — send it in the reply.

Next steps on our side: Ill loop in the interviewing team to pick reviewer slots for scoring next week. Lauren and Marissa — can you both confirm availability to review on Tuesday/Wednesday? Mina, looped for a potential tie-breaker.

Please let me know if any of the instructions are unclear. Looking forward to reading this.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Recruiter, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Work sample handoff: prompt, rubric, and reviewer scheduling

Hi Rachel —

Thanks for sending this over and for the clear rubric. Quick clarifying question: the prompt mentions handling up to ~10k short documents in memory — is the expectation that the prototype demonstrates full-scale ingestion, or are design notes + a small sample dataset acceptable? I want to scope the prototype so I can deliver a useful artifact by Monday.

Also, is it okay to use an external library (e.g., Faiss) for the prototype, or should everything be implemented from scratch?

Thanks — Ill plan for the write-up + a light prototype unless you advise otherwise.

Best,
Samir
(samir.patel@gmail.com, +1 415-555-0182)
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@gmail.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Feb 2027 12:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Work sample handoff: prompt, rubric, and reviewer scheduling

Hi Samir —

Great questions — thanks for checking. Short answers:
- Prototype scope: design notes + a focused prototype on a small sample dataset are perfectly fine. Were evaluating your design reasoning and trade-offs first; the prototype is there to show concrete choices.
- Libraries: using standard libraries like Faiss or Annoy is totally acceptable; please call out where youve relied on external tooling and any trade-offs that implies.

If you need more time beyond Monday, tell me how much and why, and well consider a short extension.

Good luck — looking forward to it.

Rachel
Recruiter, Redwood Inference
